description: In the early 1800’s, trappers would assemble at “rendezvous” to trade furs for goods. Relive the spirit of the early rendezvous this Memorial Day weekend at the 25th annual Chichaqua Rendezvous on May 29-31. The event is free to the public! Activities begin at 9 a.m. & conclude at 6 p.m. on Saturday and Sunday & at 3 p.m. on Monday. The rendezvous features more than 40 camps of “freeskinners”, or trappers who worked independently of the giant fur-trading companies. It recreates the years between 1820 - 1840, when the fur trade was at its height in the land which later became Iowa. The public is invited to attend the event & watch the “freeskinners” compete against each other in shooting muzzleloaders, throwing tomahawks, starting fires using flint & steel, and blacksmithing. Dress up in period clothes to compete in the above freeskinner activities & win prizes. A kid’s fishing derby will also be held. Crafts will be on display, including scrimshaw, beadwork, cloth & leather goods. On Sunday at 2:30 p.m., a camp auction of primitive & non-primitive items donated by companies all over the country will be held for the public. Chichaqua Bottoms Greenbelt is located in northeast Polk County about 8 miles east of the Elkhart exit on Interstate 35. For more information on the rendezvous, call Chip Collins at (515) 778-2315 or Deanna Major at (515) 720-8291 or go to the Chichaqua Freeskinners webpage at http://angelfire.com/ultra/buckskinning.

description:
The State Historical Museum will be “Going Places” when it opens a National Endowment for the Humanities exhibit that explores society’s transition from horse-drawn carriages to automobiles.



“Going Places” opens May 15 through August 11 at the State Historical Museum. Hours are 9 a.m.-4:30 p.m. Tuesday-Saturday & 12-4:30 p.m. Sunday.



“This exhibit takes visitors back to a time when carriages – not cars – ruled the road,” Iowa Department of Cultural Affairs Director Cyndi Pederson said. “I encourage all Iowans with an interest in the history of transportation to see this wonderful exhibit.”



Carriages – the forerunners of automobiles & trucks – were essential to American life in the 1800s. Carriages came in an assortment of sizes, shapes & finishes, from the buckboard phaeton to the sidebar buggy to the booby hut.



Visitors to the museum will experience diverse artifacts – including a full-sized carriage, children’s carriages, & assorted harnesses & tack – that speak about society’s desire for travel, speed & new technology.



The exhibit also covers a broad range of questions: How were carriages made & repaired? Where were they sold & who could afford them? The answers are surprising & frequent parallels to today’s car culture make “Going Places” a fascinating journey.



The exhibit explores the culture, evolution and eventual demise of horse-drawn transportation from the early 19th century, through the industrial revolution & into the 1900s and the dawn of the automobile age.


“Going Places” was curated by William F. Ayres, of the Long Island Museum of American Art, History, and Carriages. The exhibition has been made possible by NEH on the Road, a special initiative of the National Endowment for the Humanities. It is toured by Mid-America Arts Alliance. Founded in 1972, Mid America is a nonprofit regional arts organization based in Kansas City, Missouri. For more information, visit www.maaa.org and www.nehontheroad.org.
name: Going Places Exhibit

A unique, must-see theatre event that is guaranteed to start a conversation. Three plays in repertory by one of the most important new voices in American theatre. The New Yorker calls Neil LaBute “the best new playwright to emerge in the past decade … a genius." Together, they deal with the complexities of romantic relationships, sexual politics and physical appearance. Comprising a trilogy of plays linked by theme, though without recurring characters or a connected plot, the plays each reflect on their common themes in unique and distinctive ways. Though each play has had immensely successful productions in New York and London, the three plays have never been performed in a three-week repertory format. For more information:  www.stagewestiowa.com.

description: The exhibit traces the history of ACT, Inc. – originally known as American College Testing Program – to a meeting of co-founders E.F. That event founded the American College Testing Program, now known as ACT, Inc. Designed by Botanical Center horticulturist, Angie Buchanan, the summer gardens include a 16-foot caterpillar and larger-than-life ladybugs that greet you as you walk into the tropical Dome. Visitors will also learn about the benefits of insects as they walk through the Dome. The Botanical Center will host an event, Buggy About Plants, on Saturday, June 6, from 12:00 to 4:00 p.m. Have fun while learning about honeybees from the USDA and butterflies from Des Moines’ Butterfly Lady, Kathy Ziemer. Enjoy hands-on activity by holding live insects from the Blank Park Zoo. Visitors can also help with the annual ladybug release in the Dome. Enjoy the creativity of AJ’s Copper Garden sculptures, including giant copper bugs and butterflies placed throughout the Botanical Center and inside the Dome. Throughout 2010, visitors to the Des Moines Botanical & Environmental Center will be welcomed with a new horticultural and educational experience as the gardens transform throughout the year, all inspired by popular children’s stories, including Dr. Seuss, Charlie Brown and Eric Carle books. “Story Time in the Gardens” includes seven plant bed changes in the Dome – many bringing the stories alive with life-size props – educational activities, theme-related gift shop items, Riverwalk Café menu choices and special events, all inspired by children’s books. The theme continues into the Show House, with four unique, seasonal designs, and outside to the Herb Garden which is open May through September. Please visit the Des Moines Botanical & Environmental Center throughout the year to see each new garden.

description: Three sprint cars from the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame & Museum in Knoxville & several racing-related artifacts from the museums’ collections are on display through September in honor of the Knoxville National Sprint Car Championships, held each August since 1961. Auto racing has become the most popular spectator sport in the country & people can see these cars/artifacts up close this summer at the museum. A description of the sprint cars on display: A winged sprint car built in 2010 by Barry Jackson of JEI Chassis & owned by Lonny Parsons. The 1000-pound, 900-horsepower machine features an engine built by Paul Kistler & it competes full-time on the World of Outlaws (WoO) Sprint Car Series nationally. The car is sponsored by Casey’s General Stores, which has been a proud supporter of the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame. Danny Lasoski, Lonnie Parsons & the entire Casey’s General Stores team will compete in the 50th annual Goodyear Knoxville Nationals at Knoxville Raceway, Aug. 11-14, with an identically-prepared car. A “big car” built in 1932 by Gene Dodd of Rockford, Illinois. Dodd was a stone mason by trade, but he learned casting & machining from his father & was able to manufacture his own parts. This car raced with the Mississippi Valley Auto Racing Association (MVARA) on many dirt tracks. The car was driven by many drivers, including Darvin “Shorty” Burkholder, Danny Kladis, Ray Duckworth, Quent Cowles & Allen “Dutch” Morehouse, who tragically lost his life in the car in 1953 at the Henry County Fairgrounds dirt track in Mount Pleasant. The car was donated to the museum by Robert & Dr. Barbara Woodward of Dubuque. A super-modified car built in 1959 by National Sprint Car Hall of Famer Earl Wagner & powered by Harold “Slim” Gutknecht-prepared 364 & 401-cubic-inch engines. The car, which features a home-made intake manifold, was driven by Earl Wagner of Pleasantville and raced at numerous tracks in Iowa, including Knoxville, Des Moines (Iowa State Fairgrounds) & Oskaloosa. The Earl Wagner/“Slim” Gutknecht combo finished the Knoxville Raceway season points as champion in 1959 & runner-up in 1960 with “The Pink Lady.” In addition, the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame & Museum & the State Historical Museum have several racing-related artifacts on display, including posters & promotional materials from the movie “Fever Heat,” which was filmed in Iowa in 1968.
name: Sprint Car Exhibit

Australian birds expected to be at the Zoo include Sulfur Crested Cockatoos, Citron Crested Cockatoos, Silver Gulls, Emu, Wonga Pigeons, Diamond Doves, Cockatiel, Parakeets, Swainson Lories, Kookaburra, Eclectus Parrot, Australian Raven, Peregrine Falcon, Sarus Cranes, Corella Cockatoos, and Galah Cockatoo. “Australia has a unique and diverse population of birds and guests will be amazed by these animals and will learn about important efforts to protect these birds for future generations,” said Krathwohl. In addition to Australian birds, also expected to be at the Zoo is one of Krathwohl’s huge Andean Condors. Krathwohl has been a professional bird trainer for over 25 years and has appeared on Leno, Letterman, Animal Planet, The Discovery Channel, and many other major television networks. He has also established the only educational free flight bird show in the popular resorts of Las Vegas. Through the work of his foundation, The World Center for Exotic Birds, Inc., Krathwohl is pursuing the conservation of Andean Condors through a breeding and releasing program. Along with The Birdman Birds Down Under Bird Show, new to the Blank Park Zoo this year is the Feed a Parakeet experience as well as a mob of wallaby joeys, nine new ostrich, a pair of lesser kudu, baby goats and a hooded pitta. “Its time to gather the whole flock and soar to the Zoo,” said Mark Vukovich, CEO of the Blank Park Zoo. “The Birdman was such a success last year that we are excited about bringing him back with an all new show.” There will be two shows daily at 1pm and 3pm and three shows on the weekends at 11am, 1pm and 3pm. The show is free with paid admission to the Zoo. The show will run through August 15.
name: The Birdman's 'Birds Down Under' Bird Show

description:
This year's Clive Festival will team with an installment of the Jazz in July concert series.
"Families can come and truly enjoy themselves at no expense - from the music through Jazz in July to the kids' corner," said Clive Festival marketing chair Julie Cirksena. She added that the kids' corner includes crafts, story time and a mime show.
"The only charge is for beverages, which is how we make money for the next year's event. Any additional money we raise is given away to community groups that have helped us with the Clive Festival.
This is a family event - kids can attend the kids' corner, inflatables and much more. There will also be crafts and a game truck with all kinds of video games.
For more information or to register for the run, please go to www.clivefestival.com.
The fun starts at 5 p.m. Friday, when there will be free music featuring Faculty Lounge, a Clive After Five 25-year reunion, a tug-of-war event & the kids' corner.
The festival continues Saturday afternoon, when the mayor's 17.5-mile bike ride will take off at 2 p.m. from the Clive Aquatic Center parking lot. The route travels south to the Jordan Creek Trail in West Des Moines, east to the Bill Riley Trail & the Walnut Creek Trail before returning to the aquatic center via the Greenbelt Trail.
The fee for the ride is $20 - adults, $10 ages 10 & under & includes a T-shirt.
"We're excited about the bike ride - we love our greenbelts. I think it'll be a great way to kick-start the day," Cirksena said.

Once the ride wraps up, there will be an art show, wine tasting and the Jazz in July concert showcasing Foxboro and One Night Stand.

From 7 to 9 p.m. Saturday, Clive residents can swim for free at the aquatic center. The kids' corner will run from 4 to 8 p.m.

There will be inflatables with wristbands sold for $5 each, the Iowa Pork Producers will be selling special pork burgers, and the fun wraps up with the eighth annual fireworks display starting at approximately 9:30 p.m.

description:
The Science Center of Iowa will host "Da Vinci: The Genius," the most comprehensive exhibition ever assembled about famed Italian artist, inventor & scientist Leonardo da Vinci. The 15,000-square-foot traveling exhibition, scheduled to open Oct. 2, will be the largest SCI has ever housed in its 40-year history.

"This is an exhibition of international quality," said Paul Jennings, SCI's president & CEO. "We feel very proud to bring this exhibition to the Science Center of Iowa." The exhibition, which will run through Jan. 16, 2011, is expected to draw 50,000 visitors from a multistate area.

The exhibition, which took 10 years to create, features an array of full-scale machine inventions crafted by Italian artisans based on Da Vinci's personal notebooks, as well as reproductions of his most famous artworks, including the "Mona Lisa," "Virgin of the Rocks" & "The Annunciation." Among other elements of the exhibition are 3-D interactive presentations of "The Last Supper," the "Vitruvian Man" & the Sforza Horse sculpture.

The Da Vinci exhibition "was created to celebrate Leonardo da Vinci's great works & place them all together in a single location where people can come to marvel at the brilliance of this great mind," said Bruce Peterson, founder & managing director of Grande Exhibitions, the Australia-based company that developed the exhibition, in a press release.

A scaled-down version of the exhibition is currently on display at the National Geographic Museum in Washington, D.C. The full exhibition that SCI will host has also been on display in San Francisco, Tampa, Fla., and Portland, Ore., as well as in England, Hungary and Taiwan. Des Moines will be the smallest U.S. city in which the exhibition will appear, said Chris Kramer, SCI's vice president of development. "We had to convince Grande Exhibitions that we could handle it," he said.



SCI plans to build a new wall and entrance for the exhibition, which will be housed on the main floor between the escalators. Kramer declined to state SCI's investment to bring the exhibition to Des Moines; he said that those contract details are confidential, but that SCI expects to recoup the costs through ticket sales and sponsorships. .



Online ticket sales begin today for SCI members and on Monday for nonmembers. A "Genius Package" that includes all-day admission to the Science Center and a timed ticket to the exhibition will cost $17.75 for adults, $12 for children ages 2-12 and $15.75 for seniors. The estimated visiting time inside the exhibition is two hours, and audio tours will be available for $3. For more information or to purchase tickets, visit www.davincithegenius.com or call 274-6868.
name: Da Vinci: The Genius Exhibition

description: Ira Glass is the host and producer of the public radio program This American Life. The show had its premiere on Chicago's public radio station WBEZ in late 1995 and is now heard on more than 500 public radio stations each week by over 1.8 million listeners. Most weeks, the podcast of the program is the most popular podcast in America. Ira Glass began his career as an intern at National Public Radio's network headquarters in Washington, DC in 1978, when he was 19 years old. Over the years, he worked on nearly every NPR network news program and held virtually every production job in NPR's Washington headquarters. He has been a tape cutter, newscast writer, desk assistant, editor, and producer. He has filled in as host of Talk of the Nation and Weekend All Things Considered. Under Glass's editorial direction, This American Life has won the highest honors for broadcasting and journalistic excellence, including several Peabody and DuPont-Columbia awards. The American Journalism Review declared that the show is "at the vanguard of a journalistic revolution." It has won critical acclaim and attracted continuous national media attention over the years. In 2001, Time magazine named Glass "Best Radio Host in America." In 2009, the Corporation for Public Broadcasting awarded Glass the Edward R. Together, Big Bird, Elmo and Hu Hu Zhu locate the Big Dipper, the North Star and the Moon in the night sky. Elmo and Hu Hu Zhu want to learn more about the Moon, so Big Bird suggests that they use their imagination to travel there. Once on the Moon, Elmo and Hu Hu Zhu quickly learn that the Moon has a very different environment than Earth. description: Conscious Intention, an exhibition of new work by Sharon Booma will be on display at Olson-Larsen Galleries from September 24 through November 27. The gallery will host an opening reception on Friday, September 24, from 5 to 9 p.m. part of artstop, a citywide celebration of visual and performing arts. artstop, Friday, September 24 from 5 to 9 p.m. and Saturday, September 25 from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m., includes the Historic East Village, Court Avenue, Historic Valley Junction, Roosevelt Cultural District, Ingersoll Avenue and Western Gateway. This free, Metro-wide, arts celebration will feature 41 galleries, artists’ studios, a museum and a sculpture park. Participants are encouraged to ride the bus from district to district free of charge on Saturday. Please visit www.artstopinfo.com for more information and for a schedule of special events. Sharon Booma’s abstract mixed media work features luxurious surfaces that are made up of layers of oil paint, metal, sand, photo transfers and wax. Sharon sees her artwork as a pursuit of balance between “the tangible materials that surround us and the ungraspable spiritualism that defines us as individually unique people”. Sharon is a full-time artist living in Massachusetts. She has been exhibiting her artwork nationwide since 1986, with solo shows at LewAllen Contemporary in Santa Fe, Caldwell Snyder Gallery in San Francisco, Arden Gallery in Boston and Anderson O’Brien Fine Art in Omaha. Sharon graduated from the University of Connecticut School of Fine Arts and also studied at the College of New Rochelle in New York. Her work has been reviewed in ArtNews and Art in America.
name: Conscious Intention by Sharon Booma

The Downtown Farmers’ Winter Market will be held the third weekend of November & December inside Capital Square & outdoors at Nollen Plaza in Downtown Des Moines. The location for the Winter Market is only half a block north of the current farmers’ market location. This is the fifth year for the additional markets to be offered.

This Market is a perfect opportunity to stock up for holiday meals, parties & gift giving. More than 120 vendors will be present. Farmers will be selling a variety of locally raised products including eggs, beef, pork, duck, turkeys, holiday hams & of course, produce - there will be a variety of late season & greenhouse produce available. Shoppers can also expect to find an abundance of fresh homemade products including locally produced honey, jams, salsa, wine, cheese, soy nuts, homemade noodles, baked breads, pies & cinnamon rolls. Market patrons will also find beautiful winter flowers such as poinsettias, fresh cut Christmas trees, hand-made holiday ornaments and home decorations at these festive farmers markets.

The heart of the Downtown Farmers’ Market – Winter Season is a celebration of local food. Patrons will also enjoy the market ambiance created especially to celebrate harvest, winter, and the holiday season. The farmers’ markets will features a wide variety of holiday activities for the entire family, including musicians playing holiday music, strolling carolers, and artist demonstrations, kids’ activities & more.

description: After being beaten numerous times, Doug decided to find a way out of his predicaments. Ah ha, make them laugh.... Nobody wants to hit the funny guy. Wrong, they will still hit you. Doug honed his comedy craft at school, at home, in the bathroom, at the old folks home, in front of a mirror. Basically wherever he could get the attention he so desperately craves. Finally he decided to take his talent to the stage, to see if the masses thought he was as funny as his dog did. To which they did, Doug won the King of Comedy contest for Eastern Iowa in the summer of 2008. From there it has been nothing but up, working with some of The nations best comics. Growing up in Cedar Rapids was a great place to imitate the voices he always heard in his head. And to listen over & over to his favorite comedian Jonathan Winters album. Whether the voices were telling him to shoot out the windows in his grandma's barn or to duck out of the way of his dad's fist when he found out about the windows. Either way he has got vocal impressions down pat. Doug will have you laughing with his interpretations of the trials & tribulations of everyday life. He will tell you about the beauty of potty training his kids all way down to potty training himself when he drinks to much. Do yourself a favor and catch the show. You won't be disappointed.

Livingstone’s questions force all three women to re-examine the meaning of faith and the power of love leading to a dramatic, compelling climax. A hit on Broadway and later on film. See what the New York Times has called an outstanding play that “deals intelligently with questions of religion and psychology” and what the New York Post has called “unquestionably blindingly theatrical.”

description:
In a plantation house, a family celebrates the sixty-fifth birthday of Big Daddy, as they sentimentally dub him. The mood is somber, despite the festivities, because a number of evils poison the gaiety: greed, sins of the past and desperate, clawing hopes for the future spar with one another as the knowledge that Big Daddy is dying slowly makes the rounds. Maggie, Big Daddy’s daughter-in-law, wants to give him the news that she’s finally become pregnant by his favorite son, Brick. But Brick won’t cooperate in Maggie’s plans and prefers to stay in a mild alcoholic haze the entire length of his visit. Maggie has her own interests at heart in wanting to become pregnant, of course, but she also wants to make amends to Brick for an error in judgment that nearly cost her her marriage. Swarming around Maggie and Brick are their intrusive, conniving relatives, all eager to see Maggie put in her place and Brick tumbled from his position of most-beloved son.


Atkinson’s review in the NY Times called it “a stunning drama…It is the quintessence of life. It is the basic truth… CAT ON A HOT TIN ROOF is a delicately wrought exercise in human communication… As the expression of a brooding point of view about life, CAT ON A HOT TIN ROOF is limpid and effortless. As theatre, it is superb.”
name: Cat On A Hot Tin Roof

description: The works of Kim Hutchison combine her loves of sewing and painting. Kim stitches together sections of found fabric and canvas and paints colorful abstract paintings on the pieced-together surface. Kim lives in Des Moines and holds a B.A. in Visual Arts from Grandview College. Her work is in the collections of Farm Bureau Financial Services, Hy-Vee Inc., and Marshalltown Medical and Surgical Center. She was also chosen to create a commission through a competitive process for the Marshalltown Public Library in 2009. Inspiration for Brian Roberts’ work comes from his agricultural background managing a family farm for many years. His stoneware sculptures reference the familiar architectural icons of the farm – silos, grain elevators, barns and sheds. Brian is an Associate Professor of Art at Central College in Pella, Iowa. He has a B.A. from Central College, a M.A. in Art Education from Iowa State University, and a M.F.A. in both sculpture and metals from Miami University in Oxford, Ohio. His work has been in solo and group exhibitions across the country. Lee Emma Running’s interest lies in the inherent beauty of stems, stalks, roots and leaves. She uses projection, tracing, stenciling and cutting to create subtle meditations on nature and often uses dyes from plants and other natural materials as her medium. Lee is an Assistant Professor of Art at Grinnell College. She has shown her work at many venues across the country and is in the process of completing a major site-specific commission at Grinnell Regional Medical Center. Lee has completed residencies at Jentel Artists Residency in Wyoming and The Vermont Studio Center.
name: New Work by Kim Hutchison, Brian Roberts and Lee Emma Running

All donations directly benefit Food Bank of Iowa, celebrating their 30th year of service to Iowa!

description: A documentary film about one-room country schools and how they transformed rough-hewn pioneers and multilingual immigrants into a literate and patriotic new nation makes its world premiere this month in Des Moines. Country School: One Room – One Nation, written and produced by award-winning filmmakers Tammy and Kelly Rundle (Villisca: Living with a Mystery and Lost Nation: The Ioway), will be screened Nov. 19-21, at the State Historical Building. One-room country schools played a significant and prominent role in Iowa’s past and they remain a source of interest today. Many Iowans either attended a country school or had a relative who did. This film will bring back cherished memories for everyone whose lives were touched by a part of rural Midwestern education that simply doesn’t exist anymore. A list of movie times and programs follows: Nov. 19, 2010 - Premiere Event – 5:30-11 p.m. Country School will be shown at 6 p.m. and 8 p.m. Tickets are $10 per person through www.Midwestix.com. A Q & A panel discussion will follow both premiere event screenings and include the Rundles, one-room school scholar Bill Sherman, and others involved in the film. Children’s activities, entertainment by Just 4 Fun, holiday music by local Girl Scout troops, and historical country school memorabilia will be on display. DCA will also host its 6th Annual Chili for Charity fundraiser 5-8 p.m. for the Food Bank of Iowa. Chili for Charity tickets are an additional $5 payable on-site only. Nov. 20 - Country School will be shown at 2 p.m., 4 p.m., and 7 p.m. Tickets are $8 per person only at the door. Nov. 21 - Country School will be shown at 2 p.m. Tickets are $8 per person only at the door. From the first schools in new states to the demise of their widespread use in the 1950s and 1960s, Country School takes viewers back to school for a dramatic new look at the lasting impact of America's one-room schools. The visually stunning film features a unique country school designed by Frank Lloyd Wright along with dozens of more traditional structures of brick, stone or wood – in all stages of restoration or decay – in picturesque rural areas of Iowa, Kansas, Wisconsin, Missouri and Nebraska. In creating this film, producers also wanted to focus on stories that were handed down from one generation to another. They found a treasure trove of memories that are full of nostalgia, drama, humor and often heart-wrenching situations. Shot in the midst of all four seasons, the film features interviews with a who’s who of one-room school scholars, including authors Bill Samuelson, Jerry Apps, Dorothy Schwieder, Mark Dewalt, Vera Hurst, Frank Yoder and Bill Sherman, as well as former country school teachers and students. The running time of the film is approximately 80 minutes.
name: Country School: One Room, One Nation

description:
The Science Center of Iowa is hosting "Da Vinci: The Genius," the most comprehensive exhibition ever assembled about famed Italian artist, inventor & scientist Leonardo da Vinci. The 15,000-square-foot traveling exhibition is the largest SCI has ever housed in its 40-year history.

The exhibition, which will run through Jan. 16, 2011, is expected to draw 50,000 visitors from a multistate area. It took 10 years to create, features an array of full-scale machine inventions crafted by Italian artisans based on Da Vinci's personal notebooks, as well as reproductions of his most famous artworks, including the "Mona Lisa," "Virgin of the Rocks" & "The Annunciation." Among other elements of the exhibition are 3-D interactive presentations of "The Last Supper," the "Vitruvian Man" & the Sforza Horse sculpture.

The Da Vinci exhibition "was created to celebrate Leonardo da Vinci's great works & place them all together in a single location where people can come to marvel at the brilliance of this great mind," said Bruce Peterson, founder & managing director of Grande Exhibitions, the Australia-based company that developed the exhibition.

A scaled-down version of the exhibition is currently on display at the National Geographic Museum in Washington, D.C. The full exhibition that SCI will host has also been on display in San Francisco, Tampa & Portland, as well as in England, Hungary & Taiwan. Des Moines will be the smallest U.S. city in which the exhibition will appear.

Tickets are $17.75 for adults, $12 for ages 2-12 & $15.75 for seniors. The estimated visiting time inside the exhibition is two hours & audio tours will be available for $3. For more information or to purchase tickets, visit www.davincithegenius.com or call 274-6868.
name: Da Vinci: The Genius Exhibition

description: The 25th Silver Anniversary Games will take place in West Des Moines in June 2011. Softball & Cycling will get things under way the weekend of June 3–4 with the bulk of the Games taking place Thursday – Sunday, June 16–19, 2011. Registration for the Games will open in March, 2011. 2010 was a record year for participation & awards at the Iowa Senior Olympics. Nearly 1,900 medals were handed out for 68 events in 23 sports. This year we will be adding a new sport, Pickleball. Pickleball is a racquet sport, played as singles or doubles. It is a combination of tennis, badminton & table tennis played with wooden paddle racquets & a plastic, whiffle type, ball. It is played on a badminton size court with the net on the ground. Pickleball can be played indoors or outdoors. There are leagues with over 70 players in Iowa City & we expect a good number of entrants. West Des Moines Parks & Recreation hosts Pickleball during open gym. For more information on the sport, check out the National Pickleball website. http://usapa.org/ Cedar Rapids Will Host a Regional Senior Games with a great opportunity to get competition in prior to the State Games. Cedar Rapids, with the backing of the Iowa Senior Olympics, will host a two-day competition May 13-14. This competition will be open to anyone & will be held on the Coe College campus. This event will help us spread the word about competition for people over 50 & bring more people to the State Senior Olympics the folowing month. We encourage you to take advantage of the extra competition, have fun, win some medals & make new friends. Tentatively the Cedar Rapids Senior Games will host Pickleball, Swimming, Shuffleboard, Table Tennis, Tennis, Track & Field & some Board Games. Please check back at www.iowaseniorgames.org for more details!

description: Fusing the 3000 year-old tradition of Chinese acrobatic arts with the multidisciplinary approach of Cirque du Soleil, Dralion draws its inspiration from Eastern philosophy and its never-ending quest for harmony between humans and nature. The show’s name is derived from its two emblematic creatures: the dragon, symbolizing the East, and the lion, symbolizing the West. In Dralion, the four elements that govern the natural order take on a human form. Thus embodied, each element is represented by its own evocative colour: air is blue; water is green; fire is red; earth is ochre. In the world of Dralion, cultures blend, Man and Nature are one, and balance is achieved. The name Dralion (pronounced “Drah-lee-on”) is drawn from its two main symbols: the dragon, representing the East, and the lion, representing the West. Dralion derives much of its inspiration from Eastern philosophy with its perpetual quest for harmony between humankind and nature. The international cast features 52 world-class acrobats, gymnasts, musicians, singers and comedic characters.

description: One of America’s most prolific comedians of all time, Bill Cosby has dazzled generations of fans with his comedy routines, also captured on his iconic albums and best-selling books such as Fatherhood and the groundbreaking The Cosby Show. His comedy transcends age, gender, and cultural barriers. Cosby broke television’s racial barrier with a role in I Spy, becoming the first African American to costar on a television series and win three consecutive Emmys for “Outstanding Lead Actor” in the dramatic series. The veteran comic hosted the Emmy-winning cartoon Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids, which began airing in the 1970s and was made into a film in 2004. The show, based on Cosby’s childhood in Philadelphia, was designed to educate and entertain. The former Navy serviceman’s illustrious list of accomplishments includes roles on the children’s educational show Electric Company, and creating and producing the Emmy award wining Little Bill, which is based on his bestselling book series. Perhaps Cosby’s greatest contribution to American entertainment and culture is The Cosby Show, about a close-knit, upper class black family. Cosby said his intent was to portray an American family. Time magazine called the show “an encouraging sign of maturity in matters of race.” The Cosby Show dominated the No. One spot for years, earning nearly unanimous critical praise. Life magazine described the program as “a gentle, whimsical, warmhearted” show whose “delicious ordinariness of its pleasures and tribulations has given millions a fresh, laughter-splashed perspective on their own domestic lives.” For his philanthropic efforts and positive influence as a performer and author, Cosby was honored with a 1998 Kennedy Center Honors Award. In 2002, he received the Presidential Medal of Freedom, America’s highest civilian honor and the 2009 recipient of the Mark Twain Prize for American Humor. Please note: only children age 5 and over with tickets will be allowed into the theater for this production.

Her book, DAVIS COUNTY, IOWA, was just published, http://www.blurb.com/books/1547268 and she recently illustrated the new children’s book, The Red, White, and Blue Birdhouse written by Judy Combs http://debbaughmanpaintings.blogspot.com/. description:
Is there an image more vivid in the imagination of the musical public than the bewigged child Mozart
making his progress across the European continent on a succession of royal and imperial laps?
Probably not. But why would that celebrated idol be sharing a program with a 20th century victim of
Nazi-forced labor camps and Soviet bureaucratic coercion. In fact, there are some striking similarities
in the artistic development of each man.  
Mozart’s early travels involved much more than the obvious performance and applause. Everywhere
he went, the young musician looked, listened, and above all, soaked up whatever, and whomever
came his way.  Nothing and no one escaped his notice, and all was inevitably absorbed into that
glorious musical consciousness.

description:
In a plantation house, a family celebrates the sixty-fifth birthday of Big Daddy, as they sentimentally dub him. The mood is somber, despite the festivities, because a number of evils poison the gaiety: greed, sins of the past and desperate, clawing hopes for the future spar with one another as the knowledge that Big Daddy is dying slowly makes the rounds. Maggie, Big Daddy’s daughter-in-law, wants to give him the news that she’s finally become pregnant by his favorite son, Brick. But Brick won’t cooperate in Maggie’s plans and prefers to stay in a mild alcoholic haze the entire length of his visit. Maggie has her own interests at heart in wanting to become pregnant, of course, but she also wants to make amends to Brick for an error in judgment that nearly cost her her marriage. Swarming around Maggie and Brick are their intrusive, conniving relatives, all eager to see Maggie put in her place and Brick tumbled from his position of most-beloved son.

Atkinson’s review in the NY Times called it “a stunning drama…It is the quintessence of life. It is the basic truth… CAT ON A HOT TIN ROOF is a delicately wrought exercise in human communication… As the expression of a brooding point of view about life, CAT ON A HOT TIN ROOF is limpid and effortless. As theatre, it is superb.”
name: Cat On A Hot Tin Roof

Choose to greet spring with a cheerful, airy program? Or drive the accumulated energy to a musical high? Perhaps a little of both, with some adventure to taste. For youthful good spirits we need look no further than the artists themselves. Described as a “superb team,” the Amelia Trio was discovered & mentored by Isaac Stern, then quickly earned a place at festivals & major halls throughout the world.                                                                                          

But these consummate musicians have not been satisfied with the ordinary rewards of public &
critical acclaim. Nor with the standard repertoire. Masters though they are of those great scores the
world knows & loves, the Amelia’s have searched for, and commissioned a number of new
works, which share their programs with the giants of past centuries. It is not unusual, therefore, to
anticipate a program that starts with Beethoven’s great Ghost Trio, and ends with the stunning,
supremely romantic Tchaikowsky Trio.

description: Ryan's future is bright. Named one of Rolling Stone’s five comics to watch & with standout appearances on NBC's Last Comic Standing, Comedy Central's Live at Gotham & the Showtime special Caroline Rhea & Friends, he's on his way to establishing himself as one of the nation's favorite stand-ups. Ryan started life in a small, beautiful potato farming community in Idaho. While spending his youth doing things like sleeping in a tree house, riding his bike to the drug store for milkshakes & living out other Norman Rockwell paintings, he often dreamt of becoming a late night talk show host (or a secret agent, or Ferris Bueller, or Spider Man). He received his degree in journalism & public relations at Brigham Young University. Before graduating he took an internship in a small New Hampshire town and spent the weekends exploring Boston. On one trip, Ryan caught a stand-up show headlining the late Mitch Hedberg that had a profound effect and was the final push he needed to give stand up a go. Three years later, almost to the day, Ryan performed in that same Boston club as a semi-finalist in Comedy Central's Laugh Riots, one of a handful of fledgling comedians selected in a nationwide search. In his first year, he spent his nights performing in the local Salt Lake City, UT clubs and his days working in PR. He eventually decided to pursue comedy full-time and has been making a name for himself as a stand-up ever since. Early on, Ryan spent a year in Seattle, WA honing his act nightly, sleeping in his car all too often, and cutting his teeth in the notoriously difficult Northwest one-nighter bar show runs. His first break came when he won the industry night at the Seattle International Comedy Competition. He considers both Salt Lake City and Seattle comedy homes. He's become a favorite among industry insiders by racking up national competition wins and festival appearances. He most recently won the MVP award for “The Comedy Leagues” competition at the Just For Laughs Montreal Comedy Festival, garnering him a spot on the Just For Laughs Canadian cross-country tour. Previously, he won Sierra Mist's “America's Next Great Comic Search”, was a two-time finalist at the Boston Comedy Festival competition, and appeared at HBO's Las Vegas Comedy Festival as an up-and-coming talent. description:
The Science Center of Iowa is hosting "Da Vinci: The Genius," the most comprehensive exhibition ever assembled about famed Italian artist, inventor & scientist Leonardo da Vinci. The 15,000-square-foot traveling exhibition is the largest SCI has ever housed in its 40-year history.
The exhibition is expected to draw 50,000 visitors from a multistate area. It took 10 years to create, features an array of full-scale machine inventions crafted by Italian artisans based on Da Vinci's personal notebooks, as well as reproductions of his most famous artworks, including the "Mona Lisa," "Virgin of the Rocks" & "The Annunciation." Among other elements of the exhibition are 3-D interactive presentations of "The Last Supper," the "Vitruvian Man" & the Sforza Horse sculpture.
The Da Vinci exhibition "was created to celebrate Leonardo da Vinci's great works & place them all together in a single location where people can come to marvel at the brilliance of this great mind," said Bruce Peterson, founder & managing director of Grande Exhibitions, the Australia-based company that developed the exhibition.
A scaled-down version of the exhibition is currently on display at the National Geographic Museum in Washington, D.C. The full exhibition that SCI will host has also been on display in San Francisco, Tampa & Portland, as well as in England, Hungary & Taiwan. Des Moines will be the smallest U.S. city in which the exhibition will appear.
Tickets are $17.75 for adults, $12 for ages 2-12 & $15.75 for seniors. The estimated visiting time inside the exhibition is two hours & audio tours will be available for $3. For more information or to purchase tickets, visit www.davincithegenius.com or call 274-6868.
name: Da Vinci: The Genius Exhibition

description: Americana singer/songwriter Ryan Bingham was raised in rural Texas, where years of hardscrabble ranch work & rodeo competitions would later lend a sense of authenticity to his music. Living alone since a teenager, Bingham shuttled back & forth between Southwestern border towns & relatives' homes, often sleeping in his truck after rodeo shows. It was during those treks that he began entertaining friends with the guitar, an instrument he'd learned at the age of 17 from a mariachi neighbor. Drawing inspiration from Bob Dylan, Marshall Tucker & Bob Wills -- all of whom populated the jukebox of The Halfway Bar, a roadhouse owned by Bingham's uncle (whose musical tastes influenced him) -- Bingham fashioned a road-weary sound that piqued the interest of a barroom proprietor in Stephenville, Texas.

description: National Goat Exposition Set for Fall of 2012 (Oquawka, Il) â€“ The National Goat Exposition committee has been hard at work and is pleased to announce that the National Goat Expo will take place on October 7-11th, 2012 at the Iowa State Fair Grounds in Des Moines, Iowa. This 5 day event will have something for all goat breeders in a one stop format. For the dairy goat breeders there will be daily sanctioned shows (some dual) for all breeds of dairy goats. Seminars by Dr. Curtis Young, from Iowa State University, will be given on Goat Reproduction and Dr. Noah Litherland, from the University of Minnesota, will be presenting feeding information on Dry Doe and Kids in the Nursery. Demonstrations will also be given on how to use goat milk to make soap, lotion and simple cheeses. Boer goat breeders will have a sanctioned show and seminars on various topics. The other meat breeds, such as the New Zealand Kiko, Spanish, and Savanna will be showcased and seminars will be held to learn more about these increasingly popular breeds and how to raise them. The committee hasnâ€™t forgotten the fiber goats either. Several breeds of fiber goats such as Angora and Pygora will be at the exposition, along with demonstrations on how to shear and spin goat fiber into yarn will be held during the five day event. In addition to seminars, demonstrations, shows and showcases there will be vendors such as Hoegger Goat Supply and Sydell, plus many more. You will be able to purchase everything goat related. The National Goat Exposition of 2012 will certainly be a huge event for goat breeders and enthusiast that we hope to have year after year. For more information contact Jen Parrish at (515) 402-6124 or email at nationalgoatexpo@yahoo.com

The Downtown Community Alliance & the Civic Center of Greater Des Moines announce the lineup for "Lunch Unplugged," the series of shows aimed to energize downtown workers. "Lunch Unplugged" will be from 12 - 1 p.m. starting March 4 at the Temple for Performing Arts, downtown. Shows will be held weekly through April 21. 
The lineup for Lunch Unplugged includes: Friday, March 4: Ry Cuming - Ry is an Australian-born singer songwriter - think Jack Johnson meets Stevie Wonder. He is touring this spring with OneRepublic & Maroon 5. Genre: Pop/Rock/Acoustic 
Thursday, March 10: Butch Thompson - In his 40-year career, pianist Butch Thompson has earned a worldwide reputation as a traditional jazz & ragtime master. Genre: Piano, jazz/ragtime 
Thursday, March 17: Valerie Vigoda - Valerie is a singer/electric violin player & has toured the world with Cyndi Lauper when they opened for Tina Turner & Cher, Joe Jackson & the Trans-Siberian Orchestra. Genre: Electric violinist/singer/songwriter 
Friday, March 25: Vance Gilbert - Vance Gilbert burst onto the singer/songwriter scene in the early '90s when buzz started spreading in the folk clubs of Boston about an ex-multicultural arts teacher who was knocking 'em dead at open mics. Genre: Singer/Songwriter 
Wednesday, March 30: "The Magic Flute" by Opera Iowa -"The Magic Flute" is a spectacular potpourri of worldly & heavenly delights all set with sublime enchantment to some of Mozart's greatest music. Genre: Opera 
Wednesday, April 6 -- Sonos: Sonos turned a cappella on its head with bold interpretations of 21st century classics - reinventing artists like Radiohead & Fleet Foxes to the Jackson 5 & Britney Spears. If you like Glee, you'll love Sonos. Genre: A cappella/popular 
Friday, April 15 -- Catie Curtis: The vivid songwriting of Catie Curtis combines insightful lyrics with addictive melodies and energy. Her music has been featured on popular TV shows such as Grey's Anatomy, Dawson's Creek, Alias & Chicago Hope. Genre: Singer/songwriter/folk 
Thursday, April 21 -- The Nadas: A local favorite, The Nadas will feature Jason Walsmith & Mike Butterworth, the duo work perfectly as a songwriting unit, skillfully evoking the romance, introspection & uncertainty of living life on one's own terms in the 21st Century. Genre: singer/songwriters/folk/rock. 
Tickets cost $8 & can be bundled with a boxed lunch from South Union Bread Cafe for an additional $7. You may also bring a lunch to eat in the theater. Tickets can also be purchased at the venue, 30 minutes before the show. Ticket inquiries can be made by calling the Civic Center ticket office at 515-246-2300 or visiting LunchUnplugged.com.

description:
The American Institute of Architects, Iowa Chapter announces the 2011 Central Iowa Canstruction® event, a charity event committed to ending hunger making a significant contribution to the fight against HUNGER across Iowa. Central Iowa Canstruction’s 15th annual competition will be held for the first time at the Capital Square Atrium. This competition puts a visual spotlight on hunger while showcasing the design community’s best & brightest. This event is planned & presented by the American Institute of Architects, Iowa Chapter. 
Local architects, design professionals, engineers & students from area schools are challenged to design & build sculptures using canned food as their primary building material. Tape & cardboard serve as nails & cement. The colors available on product labels become the artists’ pallet. “Bricks” come in a variety of sizes from the smallest tuna can to the industrial-size tomato can. 
Teams will build “Canstructions” from 7-11 a.m., March 26. The public is invited to view the structures. Awards ceremonies will follow that day at noon. Multiple awards will be given for Best Meal, Best Use of Labels, Structural Ingenuity, Jurors’ Favorite, Honorable Mentions, Young Designer‘s & the People’s Choice. Jury members include local celebrities from Central Iowa. 
The public is encouraged to visit the displays & bring canned food for donation to the Food Bank of Iowa. This deliciously inventive charity competition will remain on display at the Capital Square Atrium through April 2. 
All food/proceeds will be donated to the Food Bank of Iowa, serving 285 agencies in 42 Iowa counties.
name: Central Iowa Canstruction

Help us celebrate & remember children from across Iowa area who have been affected by cancer. Each day, 35 children will be diagnosed with cancer. Seven of those children will lose their battle. We need to fight children’s cancer & we need your help. Walk with us to raise funds for the collaborative research efforts of the Children’s Oncology Group. 
COG hospitals treat 90% of children with cancer in the United States, providing the unmatched combination of global expertise and local care. The Children’s Oncology Group has improved survival rates for children’s cancer at a pace much faster than any one individual or institution could accomplish alone. The Children’s Oncology Group has turned cancer from a virtually incurable disease 40 years ago to one with an overall cure rate of 78%. We won't stop until we reach 100%! 
Walk with us to help reach that goal. Date: May 14, 2011. Location: Principal Park, Des Moines (the address is One Line Drive). Time: 8 am- 12 pm. Walk Cost: $10 suggested donation, but all walkers are encouraged to raise funds.

description:
Is there an image more vivid in the imagination of the musical public than the bewigged child Mozart
making his progress across the European continent on a succession of royal and imperial laps?
Probably not. But why would that celebrated idol be sharing a program with a 20th century victim of
Nazi-forced labor camps and Soviet bureaucratic coercion. In fact, there are some striking similarities
in the artistic development of each man.  
Mozart’s early travels involved much more than the obvious performance and applause. Everywhere
he went, the young musician looked, listened, and above all, soaked up whatever, and whomever
came his way.  Nothing and no one escaped his notice, and all was inevitably absorbed into that
glorious musical consciousness.  

For information on the concert series, please go to www.desmoinesartcenter.org.

How many cases does the staff typically work? How does evidence get to the lab? Get answers to your questions about the real world of forensic scientists! Moderated by Amy Pollpeter, Criminalist at the Iowa DCI Crime Lab Amy Pollpeter has a Bachelor's of Science degree in Biology from Iowa State University and Master's of Science degrees in Biology and Forensic DNA and Serology from the University of North Carolinca at Wilmington and the University of Florida. She has worked in the DNA section of the Iowa Division of Criminal Investigation Crime lab for 4.5 years and has participated in the crime scene section of the laboratory for 3.5 years. Before coming to the Iowa DCI, she worked as a research biologist at the FDA National Center for Toxicological Research in Jefferson, Arkansas.

description: Watching Mike Merryfield perform is like listening to a music aficionado's iPod set to shuffle play. The songs bounce from style to style, yet they somehow seem to fit together. One minute, Mike is talking about why maybe it isn't such a good idea for Dale Earnhardt to be God's driver. The next, he's sharing the difficulties of trying to look away from girls who wear jogging pants with words written on the backside (they do combine two of his favorite things, after all: butts and reading). It all comes together in a tight, well-crafted act that appeals to all audiences. Mike has been performing for nearly a decade, and through relentless road work his act has developed to the point where he's ready to take that next step toward the big time. He's got the complete package: an impeccable sense of timing, strong character acting and the ability to deliver jokes with multiple punchlines that keep audiences laughing. He delivers jokes in a friendly, easygoing style that goes down like a great beer on a hot summer day. Things have steadily been picking up for Mike, and he has been able to showcase his talent in a diverse array of venues. In 2003, he helped Harley-Davidson celebrate a major milestone by being the voice of its 100th Anniversary Reunion Bash, where he also performed. He also has performed from 1998 to 2002 at Summerfest, the world's largest music and entertainment festival held each year in Milwaukee. In 2004, Mike performed at the Boston International Comedy and Movie Festival and made his debut on XM and Sirius satellite radio. Mike has performed everywhere, from the Caribbean to Korea, Japan and Guam. In a business where too many performers rely on shtick or the latest political joke du jour to get laughs, Mike Merryfield is refreshingly original. His act never feels fake or forced. By simply being himself, he's become a comic on the verge of stardom.
name: Funny Bone presents Mike Merryfield

description: Chris Pureka is a breath of fresh air in an age of fleeting success and temporary notions. She is an artist of substance, armed with a sharp eye for oft-missed details and an emotional intelligence that can switch from withering to compelling with a subtle inflection. On her third release, How I Learned To See In The Dark set to hit via Sad Rabbit Music /ADA on April 13, Pureka expands on her distinct and beautiful melodies exploring broader musical soundscapes all the while maintaining the stunning vocals and distinct guitar work she is known for. With her 2004 debut LP, Driving North, Pureka started a career as a touring troubadour and began building an impressive fan base from the ground up: a cult following that started in her native New England and steadily grew to a national level. Fans and critics alike were drawn to the signature voice that somehow makes heartbreak sound desirable and her acute attention to lyrical detail, while others lauded her aptitude for crafting guitar parts that speak for themselves. The Boston Globe raved that "[she] is such a gifted guitar player and singer that you have to listen to each song twice, once for her guitar playing and again for her passionate lyrics about love, loss and hope." With her 2006 follow-up, Dryland, Pureka further expanded on the emotional topography she charted earlier in her career by continuing to tour extensively playing 200+ shows a year and gathering supporters city by city, show by show and fan by fan. This year Chris will take touring to the next level by adding a full backing band to her incredible live show.
name: Chris Pureka

description: Joe Purdy, a singer/songwriter from Arkansas, put in his time working at a loading dock and as a counselor at a private high school before his song "Wash Away" became synonymous with the 2004 season of ABC's Lost. Purdy left Arkansas for California in 2001, where he learned how to play the piano and began writing songs. He went on to record several homemade albums, breaking into the L.A. music scene with 2003's StompinGrounds. It was around this time that Purdy was contacted by J.J. Abrams, the executive producer of Lost, who asked Purdy to write a song for the show. Purdy, who at the time was visiting an island on a river in upstate New York, wrote "Wash Away," which went on to chart in the Top 25 on the iTunes country charts. The album that featured the song, Julie Blue, was released in 2004. Only Four Seasons followed it up two years later.
name: Joe Purdy

description:
The Science Center of Iowa is hosting "Da Vinci: The Genius," the most comprehensive exhibition ever assembled about famed Italian artist, inventor & scientist Leonardo da Vinci. The 15,000-square-foot traveling exhibition is the largest SCI has ever housed in its 40-year history.
The exhibition is expected to draw 50,000 visitors from a multistate area. It took 10 years to create, features an array of full-scale machine inventions crafted by Italian artisans based on Da Vinci's personal notebooks, as well as reproductions of his most famous artworks, including the "Mona Lisa," "Virgin of the Rocks" & "The Annunciation." Among other elements of the exhibition are 3-D interactive presentations of "The Last Supper," the "Vitruvian Man" & the Sforza Horse sculpture.
The Da Vinci exhibition "was created to celebrate Leonardo da Vinci's great works & place them all together in a single location where people can come to marvel at the brilliance of this great mind," said Bruce Peterson, founder & managing director of Grande Exhibitions, the Australia-based company that developed the exhibition.
A scaled-down version of the exhibition is currently on display at the National Geographic Museum in Washington, D.C. The full exhibition that SCI will host has also been on display in San Francisco, Tampa & Portland, as well as in England, Hungary & Taiwan. Des Moines will be the smallest U.S. city in which the exhibition will appear.
Tickets are $17.75 for adults, $12 for ages 2-12 & $15.75 for seniors. The estimated visiting time inside the exhibition is two hours & audio tours will be available for $3. For more information or to purchase tickets, visit www.davincithegenius.com or call 274-6868.
name: Da Vinci: The Genius Exhibition

description: A 2-for-1 theatrical presentation will be offered at the State Historical Building with one play focusing on the life & times of Henry A. Wallace & the second about the historical relationship of Roswell Garst & Nikita Khrushchev. The State Historical Museum will present "American Dreamer: The Life & Times of Henry A. Wallace" at 7 p.m. & "Peace Through Corn" at 8 p.m. Contact Maureen Korte at maureen.korte@iowa.gov or 515-281-4132 for more information. Full schedule follows: 6p.m.: Tickets, $10 per person, includes both shows available at the door, or in advance by contacting Korte 7p.m.: American Dreamer: The Life & Times of Henry A. Wallace 7:45p.m. Intermission 8p.m.: Peace Through Corn 8:45p.m.: Peace Through Corn Q & A with Liz or Rachel Garst (granddaughters of Roswell Garst). "American Dreamer" is a one-act play based on the award-winning book by Senator John C. Culver & John Hyde. Actor Tom Milligan portrays Henry A. Wallace, the agricultural innovator/founder of Pioneer Hi-Bred who became U.S. Secretary of Agriculture and, later, Vice President under Franklin Roosevelt. Admired by many & later branded as a Socialist during his controversial 1948 campaign for the presidency, Wallace always held out a vision for the future. "Peace Through Corn" brings alive the unprecedented personal friendship between Iowa farmer Roswell Garst & Soviet Union Premier Nikita Khrushchev. The production is based in part on actual dialogue as reflected in the two men's letters, memoirs & speeches. During a fearful time when the world was poised at the brink of nuclear disaster, Garst & Khrushchev forged a unique human bond based on their mutual fascination with agricultural progress & their shared love of a good laugh & a ferocious debate. Garst's personal outreach to political leaders across the Iron Curtain also represented one of the first instances of private citizen diplomacy during the post-war era. The play was written by Iowa playwright Cynthia Mercati. Khrushchev is played by actor John Earl Robinson & Garst by Michael Cornelison.
name: The Life & Times of Henry A. Wallace & Peace Through Corn

Montgomery Marilla Cuthbert and her brother Matthew request an orphan boy to help work their farm, but are mistakenly sent the high-spirited red-headed Anne Shirley. Knowing they are ill equipped to raise a child, Marilla attempts to send Anne back to the orphanage. With Matthew lobbying to keep Anne, Marilla ultimately agrees to let her stay at Green Gables. The trials and tribulations Marilla fears come to pass as Anne insults Marilla's best friend, "loses" Marilla's most cherished brooch, smacks the school's prize pupil with a slate, and inadvertently gets her best friend Diana drunk on cherry cordial. Her growing rapport with the youngsters, coupled with her generosity of spirit, gradually captures the heart of the stern Captain, and they marry. Upon returning from their honeymoon they discover that Austria has been invaded by the Nazis, who demand the Captain's immediate service in their navy. The family's narrow escape over the mountains to Switzerland on the eve of World War II provides one of the most thrilling and inspirational finales ever presented in the theatre. The motion picture version remains the most popular movie musical of all time.

Wide-eyed Scout is fascinated with the sensitively revealed people of her small town but, from the start, there's a rumble of thunder just under the calm surface of the life here. The black people of the community have a special feeling about Scout's father & she doesn't know why. A few of her white friends are inexplicably hostile & Scout doesn't understand this either. Unpleasant things are shouted & the bewildered girl turns to her father. Atticus, a lawyer, explains that he's defending a young Negro wrongfully accused of a grave crime. description: Watching Mike Merryfield perform is like listening to a music aficionado's iPod set to shuffle play. The songs bounce from style to style, yet they somehow seem to fit together. One minute, Mike is talking about why maybe it isn't such a good idea for Dale Earnhardt to be God's driver. The next, he's sharing the difficulties of trying to look away from girls who wear jogging pants with words written on the backside (they do combine two of his favorite things, after all: butts and reading). It all comes together in a tight, well-crafted act that appeals to all audiences. Mike has been performing for nearly a decade, and through relentless road work his act has developed to the point where he's ready to take that next step toward the big time. He's got the complete package: an impeccable sense of timing, strong character acting and the ability to deliver jokes with multiple punchlines that keep audiences laughing. He delivers jokes in a friendly, easygoing style that goes down like a great beer on a hot summer day. Things have steadily been picking up for Mike, and he has been able to showcase his talent in a diverse array of venues. In 2003, he helped Harley-Davidson celebrate a major milestone by being the voice of its 100th Anniversary Reunion Bash, where he also performed. He also has performed from 1998 to 2002 at Summerfest, the world's largest music and entertainment festival held each year in Milwaukee. In 2004, Mike performed at the Boston International Comedy and Movie Festival and made his debut on XM and Sirius satellite radio. Mike has performed everywhere, from the Caribbean to Korea, Japan and Guam. In a business where too many performers rely on shtick or the latest political joke du jour to get laughs, Mike Merryfield is refreshingly original. His act never feels fake or forced. By simply being himself, he's become a comic on the verge of stardom.
name: Funny Bone presents Mike Merryfield

description:
An electric guitar made from plexiglas? Pickups made out of metal lipstick tubes? How can these materials possibly make beautiful music? These are just two of the unexpected items found in 17 guitars that make up Dr. Alex King's unique collection. Dr. King will share his collection of new & vintage guitars, describe some of the unusual choices of material that guitar makers have used over the years & explain why some of those choices work better than others. Dr. King grew up in London & moved to the US after he earned his doctorate at Oxford University. He has worked at MIT, Stony Brook University & Purdue University prior to becoming the Director of the U.S. Department of Energy's Ames Laboratory at Iowa State, where he leads one of the nation's premiere materials research institutes. Dr. King has also been the president of the Materials Research Society & a science advisor in the US Dept. of State. His professional interest in materials & life-long interest in guitars combined to form his unique hobby of searching for guitars made from interesting materials. 
Cafe Scientifique is a free event for all ages & takes place on the first Tuesday of every month. No prior subject knowledge is necessary, just an interest in the topic at hand!

description:
The American Institute of Architects, Iowa Chapter announces the 2011 Central Iowa Canstruction® event, a charity event committed to ending hunger making a significant contribution to the fight against HUNGER across Iowa. Central Iowa Canstruction’s 15th annual competition will be held for the first time at the Capital Square Atrium. This competition puts a visual spotlight on hunger while showcasing the design community’s best & brightest. This event is planned & presented by the American Institute of Architects, Iowa Chapter. 

Local architects, design professionals, engineers & students from area schools are challenged to design & build sculptures using canned food as their primary building material. Tape & cardboard serve as nails & cement. The colors available on product labels become the artists’ pallet. “Bricks” come in a variety of sizes from the smallest tuna can to the industrial-size tomato can. 

Teams will build “Canstructions” from 7-11 a.m., March 26. The public is invited to view the structures. Awards ceremonies will follow that day at noon. Multiple awards will be given for Best Meal, Best Use of Labels, Structural Ingenuity, Jurors’ Favorite, Honorable Mentions, Young Designer‘s & the People’s Choice. Jury members include local celebrities from Central Iowa. 

The public is encouraged to visit the displays & bring canned food for donation to the Food Bank of Iowa. This deliciously inventive charity competition will remain on display at the Capital Square Atrium through April 2. 

All food/proceeds will be donated to the Food Bank of Iowa, serving 285 agencies in 42 Iowa counties.
name: Central Iowa Canstruction

description: Join us May 9 for the first Iowa 140 Character Conference. The key focus of the conference is on how real time technology (twitter, Facebook are two examples) is changing business, agriculture, media, education, sports, celebrity â€“ everything. There will be speakers from all over the world â€“ and local speakers too. Speakers present in 10 to 20 minute segments. The day moves quickly and lots of voices are heard. The event runs all day and costs $40 for early bird registration. Full registration cost is $60. High school and college students will be $10. For those who cannot attend in person, this conference will be live streamed on the internet. The #140conf events provide a platform for the worldwide twitter community to: listen, connect, share and engage with each other, while collectively exploring the effects of the emerging real-time internet on business. The format is unique and fast-paced. Presentations are limited to 10-20 minutes each, to permit as many people as possible to share their stories. Presenters are selected to stimulate discussion across a wide range of sectors including: business, agriculture, government, tourism, education, entertainment, non-profit and more. Since the launch of the #140conf events, conferences have taken place in a number of cities around the world. description: Cafe Scientifique is a FREE, informal science forum for adults in the Central Iowa community on the first Tuesday of every month. No prior knowledge is necessary, just an interest in the topic at hand! An electric guitar made from plexiglas? Pickups made out of metal lipstick tubes? How can these materials possibly make beautiful music? These are just two of the unexpected items found in 17 guitars that make up Dr. Alex King's unique collection.  Dr. King will share his collection of new and vintage guitars, describe some of the unusual choices of material that guitar makers have used over the years, and explain why some of those choices work better than others. Moderated by Dr. Alex King Director, U.S. Department of Energy's Ames Laboratory at ISU Dr. Alex King grew up in "Swinging London" and then moved to the US after he earned his doctorate at Oxford University. He has worked at MIT, Stony Brook University and Purdue University prior to becoming the Director of the U.S. Department of Energy's Ames Laboratory at Iowa State University, where he leads one of the nation's premiere materials research institutes. Dr. King has also been the president of the Materials Research Society, and a science advisor in the US Department of State. His professional interest in materials and life-long interest in guitars combined to form his unique hobby of searching for guitars made from interesting materials.
name: Cafe Scientifique: Bizarre Guitars

"Lunch Unplugged" will be from 12 - 1 p.m. starting March 4 at the Temple for Performing Arts, downtown. Shows will be held weekly through April 21. 

The lineup for Lunch Unplugged includes: Friday, March 4: Ry Cuming - Ry is an Australian-born singer songwriter - think Jack Johnson meets Stevie Wonder. He is touring this spring with OneRepublic & Maroon 5. Genre: Pop/Rock/Acoustic 

Thursday, March 10: Butch Thompson - In his 40-year career, pianist Butch Thompson has earned a worldwide reputation as a traditional jazz & ragtime master. Genre: Piano, jazz/ragtime 

Thursday, March 17: Valerie Vigoda - Valerie is a singer/electric violin player & has toured the world with Cyndi Lauper when they opened for Tina Turner & Cher, Joe Jackson & the Trans-Siberian Orchestra. Genre: Electric violinist/singer/songwriter 

Friday, March 25: Vance Gilbert - Vance Gilbert burst onto the singer/songwriter scene in the early '90s when buzz started spreading in the folk clubs of Boston about an ex-multicultural arts teacher who was knocking 'em dead at open mics. Genre: Singer/Songwriter 

Wednesday, March 30: "The Magic Flute" by Opera Iowa -"The Magic Flute" is a spectacular potpourri of worldly & heavenly delights all set with sublime enchantment to some of Mozart's greatest music. Genre: Opera 

Wednesday, April 6 -- Sonos: Sonos turned a cappella on its head with bold interpretations of 21st century classics - reinventing artists like Radiohead & Fleet Foxes to the Jackson 5 & Britney Spears. If you like Glee, you'll love Sonos. Genre: A cappella/popular 

Friday, April 15 -- Catie Curtis: The vivid songwriting of Catie Curtis combines insightful lyrics with addictive melodies and energy. Her music has been featured on popular TV shows such as Grey's Anatomy, Dawson's Creek, Alias & Chicago Hope. Genre: Singer/songwriter/folk 

Thursday, April 21 -- The Nadas: A local favorite, The Nadas will feature Jason Walsmith & Mike Butterworth, the duo work perfectly as a songwriting unit, skillfully evoking the romance, introspection & uncertainty of living life on one's own terms in the 21st Century. Genre: singer/songwriters/folk/rock.

description: Registration is now open for Hope Ministries' 8th annual Hearts for Hope Women's Tea, a benefit for Hope Family Center. The event is set for May 7 at the Sheraton West Des Moines Hotel. Burnham & her late husband, Martin, had been missionaries in the Philippines for 17 years when they were taken hostage by a militant group in 2001. We need to fight children’s cancer & we need your help. Walk with us to raise funds for the collaborative research efforts of the Children’s Oncology Group. 

COG hospitals treat 90% of children with cancer in the United States, providing the unmatched combination of global expertise and local care. The Children’s Oncology Group has improved survival rates for children’s cancer at a pace much faster than any one individual or institution could accomplish alone. The Children’s Oncology Group has turned cancer from a virtually incurable disease 40 years ago to one with an overall cure rate of 78%. We won't stop until we reach 100%!

description:
In a plantation house, a family celebrates the sixty-fifth birthday of Big Daddy, as they sentimentally dub him. The mood is somber, despite the festivities, because a number of evils poison the gaiety: greed, sins of the past and desperate, clawing hopes for the future spar with one another as the knowledge that Big Daddy is dying slowly makes the rounds. Maggie, Big Daddy’s daughter-in-law, wants to give him the news that she’s finally become pregnant by his favorite son, Brick. But Brick won’t cooperate in Maggie’s plans and prefers to stay in a mild alcoholic haze the entire length of his visit. Maggie has her own interests at heart in wanting to become pregnant, of course, but she also wants to make amends to Brick for an error in judgment that nearly cost her her marriage. Swarming around Maggie and Brick are their intrusive, conniving relatives, all eager to see Maggie put in her place and Brick tumbled from his position of most-beloved son.


Atkinson’s review in the NY Times called it “a stunning drama…It is the quintessence of life. It is the basic truth… CAT ON A HOT TIN ROOF is a delicately wrought exercise in human communication… As the expression of a brooding point of view about life, CAT ON A HOT TIN ROOF is limpid and effortless. As theatre, it is superb.”
name: Cat On A Hot Tin Roof

description:
Choose to greet spring with a cheerful, airy program? Or drive the accumulated energy to a musical high? Perhaps a little of both, with some adventure to taste. For youthful good spirits we need look no further than the artists themselves. Described as a “superb team,” the Amelia Trio was discovered & mentored by Isaac Stern, then quickly earned a place at festivals & major halls throughout the world.                                                                                          



But these consummate musicians have not been satisfied with the ordinary rewards of public &

critical acclaim. Nor with the standard repertoire. Masters though they are of those great scores the

world knows & loves, the Amelia’s have searched for, and commissioned a number of new

works, which share their programs with the giants of past centuries. It is not unusual, therefore, to

anticipate a program that starts with Beethoven’s great Ghost Trio, and ends with the stunning,

supremely romantic Tchaikowsky Trio.  

For information on the concert series, please go to www.desmoinesartcenter.org.

description: The classic Mel Brooks movie is ALIVE...and it's headed here! You'll have a monstrously good time at this spectacular new production, winner of the 2008 Outer Critics Circle Award and the Broadway.com Audience Award for BEST MUSICAL  Don't miss the sensational cast delivering all your favorite moments from the classic film, plus brand-new show-stopping numbers for the  stage, including "Transylvania Mania," "He Vas My Boyfriend" and “Puttin' on the Ritz."  This wickedly inspired re-imagining of the Frankenstein legend follows bright young Dr. Frankenstein (that's Fronkensteen) as he attempts to create a monster--but not without scary and hilarious complications. The brains behind the laughter is mad genius and three-time Tony® winner Mel Brooks himself--who wrote the music and lyrics and co-wrote the book- along with his record-breaking team from The Producers: five-time Tony-winning director and choreographer Susan Stroman and three-time Tony-winning writer, Thomas Meehan.

She is one of music's top concert draws, selling out all 107 dates on her wildly successful "Fearless" tour in 2009-10.

With one of the most influential & unmistakable songwriting voices of today, Prine continues to cast his perceptive eye upon the subtle complexities of the human condition, delivering his observations in his uniquely concise, illuminating compositions.


Some four decades since his remarkable debut, Prine recently released In Person & On Stage, a new live album featuring a duet with Emmylou Harris, proving he’s still at the top of his game, both as a performer & songwriter. Recently honored at the Library of Congress by US Poet Laureate Ted Kooser, he’s been elevated from the annals of songwriters into the realm of bonafide American treasures.

description:
We're gonna do it again! The 2011 80/35 music festival is set for Saturday and Sunday, July 2 and 3, 2011 at Western Gateway Park in downtown Des Moines. 

Girl Talk, the mash-up artist who mixes samples from popular rock, pop & hip-hop songs, will headline the first night of the July 2-3 festival in Western Gateway Park. "Girl Talk has the unique ability to conduct an entire crowd," 80/35 project manager Amedeo Rossi said. "He gets people waving their hands in the air and jumping around as he directs it. He's a good closer with high energy."


Girl Talk (real name: Gregg Gillis, from Pittsburgh) has become known for his energetic live shows, during which he mixes his samples live & brings groups of fan on stage to dance. He was one of the first acts announced for the inaugural 80/35 Music Festival in 2008, but dropped out due to a scheduling conflict. Gillis played a sold-out show at People's Court in January, 2009.



Eleven other bands have also been announced:

• Edward Sharpe & the Magnetic Zeros (July 2): At first, a side project by Ima Robot frontman Alex Ebert, in which he portrays Edward Sharpe, a messianic leader sent to save mankind. Accordionist, Nora Kirkpatrick, grew up in Grimes.


• Galactic (July 2): A New Orleans funk group that fuses elements of jazz, hip hop & rock. The band often tours with guest musicians, recently including Corey Glover of Living Colour, Cyril Neville of the Neville Brothers & Corey Henry of Rebirth Brass Band.



• Grace Potter & the Nocturnals (July 3): A roots rock band from Vermont that has performed with Dave Matthews, Gov't Mule & more. Potter added vocals to "You and Tequila" on Kenny Chesney's last album. The band's "Something I Want" was featured in the credits of "Tangled." Potter is also playing Saturday in the Park July 2 in Sioux City.


• Titus Andronicus (July 2): A New Jersey band with punk & shoegaze elements, known for raucous live performances. Its well-reviewed 2010 album, "The Monitor," is a concept album, loosely tied to the Civil War.



• The Giving Tree Band (July 3): An Illinois folk/alt-country band founded by brothers Eric & Todd Fink.



• Jessica Lea Mayfield (July 2): On Ohio singer-songwriter whose first 2 albums were produced by Dan Auerbach of The Black Keys. She grew up playing in her family's bluegrass band & is known for writing dark songs.


• Bitch (July 3): Electric violin & ukulele-playing folk singer from New York who has toured with Ani DiFranco.



• Poison Control Center (July 2): An Ames band that has spent the last year on the road in support of its double album "Sad Sour Future."



• Thankful Dirt (July 2): The local husband/wife folk duo of Darren & Molly Matthews.



• Parlours (July 3): Female-fronted folk pop from Des Moines featuring members of General Sherman & The Envy Corps.


• Bear Hands (July 3): Classmates of MGMT, this New York group recently released its debut "Burning Bush Supper Club" following its well received 2007 EP, "Golden.



The DMMC plans to announce another round of bands in the next few weeks, including a July 3 headliner. Nearly 50 bands will perform over two days on three stages.Ticket prices will rise to $60 for a two-day pass, or $35 per day, on May 17.

Early bird 2-day passes ($33) and VIP passes ($100) are on sale now. You can purchase tickets at www.midwestix.com.
