Join Mayor Cownie and the Dream Team on this fun bike ride and experience Des Moines as you ride through area neighborhoods and raise money for recreational trails. All proceeds from this event support Des Moines' recreational trails. Over the last 10 years this ride has raised over $100,000 for improvements to Des Moines trails. description:
Lucy Walker, director, 98 minutes, not rated

Levitt Auditorium; FREE admission!



Nominated for 2010’s Best Documentary Academy Award, WASTE LAND follows renowned artist Vik Muniz as he journeys from his home base in Brooklyn to his native Brazil & the world's largest garbage dump, Jardim Gramacho, located on the outskirts of Rio de Janeiro. There he photographs an eclectic band of catadores- or self-designated pickers of recyclable materials. Muniz's initial objective was to "paint" the catadores with garbage. However, his collaboration with these inspiring characters as they recreate photographic images of themselves out of garbage reveals both the dignity & despair of the catadores as they begin to re-imagine their lives. Walker has great access to the entire process and, in the end, offers stirring evidence of the transformative power of art and the alchemy of the human spirit.

Q & A will follow with Dina Smith, Associate Professor of English, Drake University, and Matt Garite, doctoral candidate in English at State University of New York, Buffalo.
name: Documentary Film: Waste Land

description: The State Historical Building will host a special event this month about the life and work of Jack Shelley, one of the most influential news broadcasters in Iowa history. "A Tribute to Jack Shelley" will be at 7:30 p.m. April 29, at the State Historical Building. The event is free and open to the public, and will feature historic broadcasts of Shelley on WHO radio and television, as well as excerpts from interviews he gave about his career. Several speakers will also discuss his impact on Iowa broadcasting. "Jack Shelley was respected nationally for his clear and concise reporting, his dedication to the craft of journalism, and a deep caring for his audience", said Jeff Stein, Archives of Iowa Broadcasting administrator and State Historical Society of Iowa board member. "He truly shaped what broadcast news would become in Iowa and the nation." A fixture on WHO Radio for three decades, Shelley (1912-2010) contributed to the founding of the Iowa Broadcast News Association, which honored him in 1972 by establishing the Jack Shelley Award for lifetime achievement in broadcast journalism. He was co-founder and former president of the international Radio-Television News Directors Association (now the Radio Television Digital News Association), and former president of the Associated Press Radio and Television Association. He was president of the Iowa Freedom of Information Council in 1981 and a member of an advisory committee appointed by the Iowa Supreme Court on the use of cameras and tape recorders in trials. In 1980, he received the Broadcaster of the Year award from the Iowa Broadcasters Association. Shelley began on WHO Radio in 1935, and founded the WHO-TV news department when the station went on the air in 1954. He taught broadcast journalism at Iowa State University for 17 years before retiring in 1982. SHSI, IBNA, Archives of Iowa Broadcasting and WHO Radio in Des Moines are sponsors of the event.
name: A Tribute to Jack Shelley

description: Travel south of the border as the Historic Valley Junction Foundation presents our 7th Annual Festival Cinco de Mayo on Saturday, May 7, 2011 from Noon to 10 p.m.. Located in the 200 & 300 Blocks of 5th Street in historic Valley Junction, West Des Moines, IA, visitors are invited to enjoy Mexican foods, artwork, live music, dancing and family activities. A special thank you to our sponsors: A-MAY-Zing Days, Miller Lite, Historic Valley Junction Foundation, and Engler Embroidery invites you to join us for a day of fun and festivities on Fifth Street. Inflatables, video game truck and other childrenâ€™s activities will be available with proceeds benefiting Phoenix Elementary School and The Historic Valley Junction Foundation. Scheduled entertainment includes youth dancers Los Ninos Tepeyec. Live music will be performed by crowd-favorites...Salsa Vibe and headliners Latino Pride. Celebrating the Mexican heritage of many railroad workers during the establishment years of Valley Junction, this festival is an opportunity to recognize the Mexican community who helped James Jordanâ€™s vision of bringing the railroad to the Des Moines area become a reality. In honor of our strong heritage, we will also present a proclamation and announcement of our Cinco de Mayo King and Queen. Valley Junction was established in 1846 when its first settler, James Jordan arrived. The name Valley Junction was chosen because it was located in the valley of the Raccoon River and served as the junction for the railroad. By 1900, the Chicago, Rock Island and Pacific Railroad had moved its operation to the area. After the railroad boom ended, Valley Junction slowed its pace and changed its official name to West Des Moines in 1938. Many family members of the original railroad workers still live in the Valley Junction area today. Festival Cinco de Mayo is part of A-May-Zing Days, a month-long celebration of West Des Moines. For a list of events and activities happening throughout the community in May, please visit www.amayzingdays.com.

There are numerous parking garages/lots downtown & east of the Des Moines River. Unfortunately, there will not be shuttle services available at this year's festival (to view a map of parking locations, go to the website at www.italianfestivalofiowa.com & select "Details"). Designated handicap/elderly parking is located at 111 Court Ave (Polk Co. Admin. Bldg) or 120 2nd Ave (Polk Co. Election Office). Parking is limited & on a first-come, first-served basis. The Festival grounds are handicap accessible. Drop-off service will be available at both entrances on the east & west ends of the Court Ave. Bridge. To ensure the safety/enjoyment of all attendees, please observe the following rules: 

*No outside beverages allowed. For safety reasons, glass bottles are prohibited. 

*Alcoholic beverages are sold within the Festival site to patrons 21 years & up w/valid I.D. State laws/regulations require that alcoholic beverages purchased at the Festival remain on-site. On-site security will ask you to dispose of any alcoholic beverages before you exit or enter. 

*Smoking not permitted inside any structure or in any seating area on the Italian-American Festival grounds. 

*Bicycles, skateboards, roller blades, large signs & placards which may endanger or inconvenience the public attending the Festival are prohibited on-site. 

*The Italian-American Heritage Festival reserves the right to decline admittance to anyone who violates the reasonable policies established for public safety or to restrict activities such as public address to designated areas. 

*All packages are subject to search. 

*Pets are forbidden for the safety of the pet due to the heat and the number of people. Be kind to your pets: leave them at home when you visit the Festival. Seeing-eye dogs are allowed, per city regulations. 

For more information, please contact the IAHF of Iowa, 1961 Indianola Road, Des Moines, Iowa, 50315 or through the website.

description: The Iowa Department of Economic Development is offering FREE Public Participation Training Workshops in six Iowa communities in the months of April and May. This is a unique opportunity to receive expert training regarding the importance of public participation as well as strategies for increasing local public participation in the planning and development process. The workshops, titled input plan-it, will be offered in two different formats in each community. The "Professionals Workshop" is a detailed, three-hour session designed for planning professionals, and local planning and project leaders. Professional planners attending the workshop may be eligible for 2.75 certification maintenance credits. The "Stakeholder Session" is a one-hour session for community leaders, representatives, residents and other stakeholders interested in getting the most out of public input. The sessions are presented by Jay Schlinsog from DPN and Dave Ciaccio and Nick Bowden from Community ReDesigned in cooperation with the Iowa Department of Economic Development. Together, the team's members bring more than fifty years of hands-on experience in planning, research and public participation. The presentations will share hints, tips, tools and resources to more fully engage the community in local planning processes. Please RSVP at least five days in advance to Jean Johnson, 515.725.3070, jean.m.johnson@iowa.gov
name: Public Participation Training Workshops

In Iowa, more than 14,000 children are victims of abuse & neglect annually. Eleven Iowa children died of abuse in 2010. Iowa residents have a chance to remember these children at the local Light of Hope event, which not only will honor these victims, but will also provide hope & opportunities to join in the fight against child abuse. 

Guest speakers will include Senator Matt McCoy, Forensic Interviewer Lana Herteen, HOPE! Drama Troupe and the Matins Choir of Plymouth Church.

description: Iowans for Social & Economic Development - Alliance for Business Owners' EDU-SEMINAR. Come join us for this FREE 1 hour educational opportunity! "MYSELF, My Business" with featured guest EMyth Benchmark. To truly go to work ON your business, you must see it as a separate entity. The new entrepreneur often sells them self, does the work, collects the money and repeats the procedure-they often develop habits and practices that prevent them from building the business and become trapped in creating a job for themselves. To start from the beginning with a healthy point of view about self and business that works for them, not because of them. Iowans for Social & Economic Development (ISED) provides information and resources for starting, strengthening or growing a microenterprise in Iowa. description:
The Friends of Des Moines Parks will be hosting two public programs featuring Texas A & M University's Dr. John Crompton, Distinguished Professor of Recreation, Park & Tourism Sciences, on May 4 and 6. Dr. Crompton is known worldwide for his work on the marketing & financing of leisure services & is the most published scholar in the history of both the tourism & parks and recreation fields. An energetic speaker who inspires & educates his audiences, Crompton will discuss how parks & recreation benefit the community through reduced healthcare costs & juvenile crime, improved community cohesion, increased property values & economic development, and more civic responsibility. 



The programs are being provided free of charge by the Friends of Des Moines Parks, a volunteer organization with a stated mission of Striving to become a primary advocate & information resource for parks, greenways & recreational programming in our city.

description:
One of the 20th century's most powerful, important & emotionally challenging operas, Dialogues of the Carmelites is based on a play by Georges Bernanos & was premiered at La Scala in Milan. Set against the terrifying backdrop of the French Revolution, it tells the story about a young woman of nobility who becomes a nun, against the wishes of her father & brother. Blanche de la Force is deeply afraid of the terror of the world in which she finds herself & joins the convent in an attempt to find refuge where she can live & work without fear.  And then the Revolution begins & nothing is ever the same again. This is a story about real people but told with some abstractions that reflect the fact that often what we say to each other is not exactly what we mean.


As the wheels of the Revolution turn, giants are felled & lesser people are left behind to tremble in the wake. The opera records the everyday happenings & conversations in Blanche's life as she watches those around her deal with faith & courage & those events that lead her to her own crisis of faith versus fear. The final scene stands alone & apart as one of the most powerful moments in all musical theatre. 

For information on tickets, pricing, times, go to www.dmmo.org.

description:
Andre Rieu, the world's most popular classical artist who is renowned for his energetic & festive live concerts, is returning to Des Moines for An Evening with Andre Rieu on September 17 at the Wells Faro Arena.

Tickets go on sale beginning Saturday, April 30, at 10 a.m. Purchase tickets by calling 866-55-DAHLS, visiting www.dahlstickets.com, the Wells Fargo Arena Box Office or all Dahl's Foods locations. 

An Evening with Andre Rieu will give fans what they,ve come to expect from Rieu,s North American performances: the maestro conducting his 60-piece Johann Strauss Orchestra & playing his world-famous Stradivarius violin to create a celebratory atmosphere, where fans are encouraged to get out of their seats & waltz in the aisles. People can expect a colorful concert, with beautiful melodies, waltzes, surprises, balloons, the tenors & lovely sopranos from South Africa & Australia. Known as "The King of Waltz", Andre Rieu is one of the best-selling live acts in the world. He was ranked as the #1 male performer of 2009 & earned one of the top-grossing tours of 2010, despite the 3-month postponement of concerts in the UK, Ireland, Australia & New Zealand due to a viral infection. Rieu has sold more than 30 million albums globally & has broken all classical concert records, packing stadiums & arenas with more than 700,000 adoring fans each year. 

His latest album, Forever Vienna, reached #2 on the British pop chart, the highest-ever position for a classical record. He has been certified 100-times platinum in Australia & has his own TV series in the Netherlands.

description: This compassionate play reveals friendship & fear in the age of AIDS. Not one for the outside world, Jody stays in his map store all the time. His friend, Carl begins bringing chairs into the store & leaving them there. Pretty soon, the store is littered with chairs & it is revealed that every chair was owned by someone they knew in their community who had died from the epidemic. Through Jody & Carl's interaction, the two realize how grateful they are to have such a strong lasting friendship. description:
Based on the book by L.M. Montgomery Marilla Cuthbert and her brother Matthew request an orphan boy to help work their farm, but are mistakenly sent the high-spirited red-headed Anne Shirley. Knowing they are ill equipped to raise a child, Marilla attempts to send Anne back to the orphanage. With Matthew lobbying to keep Anne, Marilla ultimately agrees to let her stay at Green Gables. The trials and tribulations Marilla fears come to pass as Anne insults Marilla's best friend, "loses" Marilla's most cherished brooch, smacks the school's prize pupil with a slate, and inadvertently gets her best friend Diana drunk on cherry cordial. She also turns out to be bright, charming, and resourceful, full of irresistible imagination. Marilla and Matthew admit she is the best thing that ever happened to them, and Anne comes to understand she is a loved, worthwhile person.

Family show; appropriate for ages 5 and up!

description: Winner of three Tony Awards including the award for BEST MUSICAL REVIVAL, this hilarious new production of LA CAGE AUX FOLLES was the biggest hit of the 2010 Broadway season, leaving audiences in stitches night after night! LA CAGE tells the story of Georges, the owner of a glitzy nightclub in lovely Saint-Tropez & his partner Albin, who moonlights as the glamorous chanteuse Zaza. When Georges' son brings his fiance's conservative parents home to meet the flashy pair, the bonds of family are put to the test as the feather boas fly! LA CAGE is a tuneful & touching tale of one family's struggle to stay together... stay fabulous... and above all else, stay true to themselves! With a glorious score of hummable melodies and a dynamite cast featuring the "notorious and dangerous Cagelles," LA CAGE is an indisputable musical comedy classic... and this extraordinary new version shows you why! Please note: only children age 5 and over with tickets will be allowed into the theater for this production.

When everyone picks names for Secret Santa, Junie B. gets stuck with Tattletale you-know-who! It's enough to fizzle your holiday spirit! Hmm . . . or is it? Maybe, just maybe, a Secret Santa gift is the perfect opportunity to give May exactly what she deserves.

Family show; appropriate for ages 5 & up!
name: Junie B in Jingle Bells, Batman Smells!

description: By Rodgers & Hammerstein The final collaboration between Rodgers & Hammerstein was destined to become the world's most beloved musical. When a postulant proves too high-spirited for the religious life, she is dispatched to serve as governess for the seven children of a widowed naval Captain. Her growing rapport with the youngsters, coupled with her generosity of spirit, gradually captures the heart of the stern Captain, and they marry. Upon returning from their honeymoon they discover that Austria has been invaded by the Nazis, who demand the Captain's immediate service in their navy. The family's narrow escape over the mountains to Switzerland on the eve of World War II provides one of the most thrilling and inspirational finales ever presented in the theatre. The motion picture version remains the most popular movie musical of all time. Musical appropriate for ages 8+.

description: Tony Award nominee John Tartaglia has certainly spread his creative wings. He starred in the acclaimed musical Avenue Q, appeared on Broadway in Shrek The Musical & in Disney's Beauty & the Beast, and created & starred in The Playhouse Disney series ''Johnny and the Sprites.'' Now, as if creative wings weren't enough, he has grown some creative gills as well, with the production of John Tartaglia's IMAGINEOCEAN. IMAGINEOCEAN is a magical undersea adventure for kids of all ages. Tank, Bubbles & Dorsel, three best friends who just happen to be fish, set out on a remarkable journey of discovery. It all starts with a treasure map. As they swim off in search of clues, they'll sing, they'll dance & they'll make new friends, including everyone in the audience. Ultimately they discover the greatest treasure of all: friendship. Jam-packed with music ranging from swing to R&B to Big Band, John Tartaglia's IMAGINEOCEAN is a blast from the first big splash to the last wave goodbye.
name: IMAGINOCEAN

description:
Based on the book by Harper Lee Scout, a young girl in a quiet southern town, is about to experience the dramatic events that will affect the rest of her life. She & brother Jem are being raised by their widower father Atticus & by a strong-minded housekeeper Calpurnia. Wide-eyed Scout is fascinated with the sensitively revealed people of her small town but, from the start, there's a rumble of thunder just under the calm surface of the life here. The black people of the community have a special feeling about Scout's father & she doesn't know why. A few of her white friends are inexplicably hostile & Scout doesn't understand this either. Unpleasant things are shouted & the bewildered girl turns to her father. Atticus, a lawyer, explains that he's defending a young Negro wrongfully accused of a grave crime. Atticus fights his legal battle with a result that is part defeat, part triumph. 

Drama appropriate for ages 13 & up.
name: To Kill A Mockingbird

description:
More than 50 years ago one musical changed theater forever. Now it's back & mesmerizing audiences once again. From the first note to the final breath, West Side Story soars as the greatest love story of all time. Directed by David Saint, using Tony Award-winning librettist Arthur Laurents' Broadway direction, West Side Story remains as powerful, poignant & timely as ever. 

The new Broadway cast album of West Side Story recently won the 2010 Grammy Award for Best Musical Show Album. The Bernstein & Sondheim score is considered to be one of Broadway's finest & features such classics of the American musical theatre as "Something's Coming," "Tonight," "America," "I Feel Pretty" & "Somewhere." 

Please note: only children age 5 and over with tickets will be allowed into the theater for this production.
name: West Side Story

description: Based on the book by EB White Stuart Little is no ordinary mouse! He was born to a family of humans and even has an older brother and a cat named Snowbell. Though he is shy and thoughtful, he is also a true lover of adventure. Stuart's greatest escapade comes when his friend, the lovely bird Margalo, disappears from her nest and this heroic little mouse ventures away from home to go in search of her. The book, by the author of Charlotte's Web, is brought to life along with all its charm, wisdom and joy.
name: Stuart Little

description: Diavolo was founded in 1992 in Los Angeles by Jacques Heim to create large-scale interdisciplinary performances which examine the funny and frightening ways individuals act with their environment. The company is comprised of dancers, gymnasts and actors who create performances collaboratively under the guidance of Heim, constantly changing the image presented to the audience. The sets created are outrageous and surrealistic and form an intrinsic part of each piece of work. Everyday items such as doors, chairs and stairways provide the back-drop for dramatic movement “ leaping, flying, twirling “ that creates metaphors for the challenge of relationships, the absurdities of life and the struggle to maintain our humanity in an increasingly technological world. Please note: only children age 5 and over with tickets will be allowed into the theater for this production.
name: Diavolo

description: It only takes a little to BE BIG! In conjunction with the beloved BIG dog’s 50th anniversary in 2012, celebrate the timeless values of Clifford’s BIG Ideas - Share, Play Fair, Have Respect, Work Together, Be Responsible, Be Truthful, Be Kind, Believe In Yourself, Be A Good Friend & Help Others. These sentiments have never been more fun as Clifford and his friends from Birdwell Island - Emily Elizabeth, Cleo and T-Bone – embark on new adventures. With memorable songs and choreography – there will be even more of him to love in this ALL NEW musical – sure to delight the entire family!
name: Clifford the Big Red Dog

description:
The Musical will explode on the Civic Center of Greater Des Moines stage February 28 - March 4 uniting breathtaking dance & the thrilling, cutthroat world of competitive cheerleading with one of the most remarkable scores in years!The team behind this explosive new show is an extraordinarily rare union of Broadway's most acclaimed, award-winning young creators. With an original libretto by Tony Award winner Jeff Whitty (Avenue Q), music/lyrics by Tony Award-winning composer Lin-Manuel Miranda (In The Heights), music by Pulitzer & Tony Award-winning composer Tom Kitt (Next to Normal), lyrics by Broadway lyricist Amanda Green (High Fidelity) & music supervision by Tony Award winner Alex Lacamoire (Wicked), BRING IT ON: The Musical is directed & choreographed by Tony Award winner Andy Blankenbuehler (In The Heights). 

Please note: only children age 5 and over with tickets will be allowed into the theater for this production.
name: Bring It On The Musical

description: A set of gifted singers and instrumentalists sing through some of the greatest songs of one of America's most brilliant singer/songwriters, Johnny Cash. Though he is never impersonated, his remarkable life story is told through his music, climaxing in a concert that will both move and exhilarate! Ring of Fire celebrates the Man in Black, Johnny Cash, and his remarkable life story is told through his music.
name: Ring of Fire

description: Moulin Rouge The Ballet has been seen by close to 60,000 people across North America and has elicited cheers and ovations. Along with a rousing French soundtrack, the ballet features high-kicking choreography and a passionate story of love, ambition and heartbreak. Turn of the century Paris,  a city of exquisite contradiction. The elixir of personal freedom bred lifestyles both reckless and addictive. Drawn to Paris by the city's passion, a flame fuelled by the hearts of lovers and the souls of poets, Matthew and Nathalie tempt fate as they seek love and destiny at the infamous cabaret The Moulin Rouge. Please note: only children age 5 and over with tickets will be allowed into the theater for this production.
name: Royal Winnipeg Ballet: Moulin Rouge - The Ballet

description: The sexy athleticism, exuberant personality and joyous movement that is Parsons Dance is comprised of 10 full-time dancers and maintains a repertory of more than 60 works (20 with commissioned scores) choreographed by David Parsons. The company's style is a fusion of the gesture and movement that make up the modern dance vocabulary, and the discipline and precise execution one expects from a classical company. Please note: only children age 5 and over with tickets will be allowed into the theater for this production.
name: Parsons Dance

description:
Three meddlesome spirits – Music, Noise and Silence – invade symphony hall. The concert seems doomed as Silence and Noise attempt to seize control of the orchestra. Only with the help of the audience and Music will the conductor be able to break the fierce grip of Noise and bring harmony back to the orchestra.

Des Moines Symphony with Magic Circle Mime Company, Joseph Giunta, conducting.
name: Music, Noise & Silence

description:
TURN UP THAT DIAL... From the underground dance clubs of 1950s Memphis, Tennessee, comes a hot new Broadway musical that bursts off the stage with explosive dancing, irresistible songs & a thrilling tale of fame & forbidden love. 

Inspired by actual events, MEMPHIS is about a white radio DJ who wants to change the world & a black club singer who is ready for her big break. Come along on their incredible journey to the ends of the airwaves -- filled with laughter, soaring emotion & roof-raising rock 'n' roll. Winner of four 2010 Tony Awards including Best Musical, MEMPHIS , which played pre-Broadway at the La Jolla Playhouse, features a Tony-winning book by Joe DiPietro (I Love You, You're Perfect, Now Change) & a Tony-winning original score with music by Bon Jovi founding member David Bryan. Directing is Tony nominee Christopher Ashley (Xanadu) & choreography is by Sergio Trujillo (Jersey Boys). 

Get ready to experience Broadway's most exciting new destination!

Please note: only children age 5 and over with tickets will be allowed into the theater for this production.
name: Memphis

description: Based on the book by Jeff Brown One night, the bulletin board on the wall above Stanley's bed comes loose and falls right on top of Stanley. The next morning, Stanley Lambchop wakes up flat. Not just a little flat...really, REALLY flat! At first it's not so bad. He can slide under locked doors, roll up like a mat, become a trampoline. His friends fly him like a kite. And Stanley's the best in his class at hide-and-seek: He just turns to the side and virtually disappears. But he can't stay flat forever - someone has to do something. And that someone in Stanley! Stanley puts himself in a big envelope and travels the world - a human letter.
name: The Musical Adventures of Flat Stanley

description:
DIRECT FROM BROADWAY! RAIN RETURNS! RAIN, the internationally-acclaimed Beatles concert, returns by popular demand! RAIN performs the full range of The Beatles' discography live onstage, including the most complex & hallenging songs that The Beatles themselves recorded in the studio but never performed for an audience. Together longer than The Beatles, RAIN has mastered every song & gesture of the legendary foursome, delivering a totally live, note-for-note performance that's as infectious as it is transporting. 

From the early hits to later classics (I Want To Hold Your Hand, Hard Day's Night, Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band, Let It Be, Come Together, Hey Jude & more), this adoring tribute will take you back to a time when all you needed was love, and a little help from your friends! 

Please note: only children age 5 and over with tickets will be allowed into the theater for this production.
name: Rain: A Tribute to the Beatles

description:
The Golden Dragon Acrobats represent the best of a time honored tradition that began more than 25 centuries ago. The Golden Dragons are recognized throughout the United States and abroad as the premiere Chinese acrobatic touring company of today.

The reputation of the company is solidly rooted in a commitment to the highest of production values and an attention to artistic details that is unparalleled in the art form. World renowned impresario Danny Chang and choreographer Angela Chang combine award-winning acrobatics, traditional dance, spectacular costumes, ancient and contemporary music and theatrical techniques to present a show of breathtaking skill and spellbinding beauty.
name: Golden Dragon Acrobats

description: A mysterious figure has arrived in town. A flurry of a cape, the glint of a sword and a flash of a mask; who is this baffling character? Exciting friend or formidable foe? If you are looking for some swash-buckling fun, come and lock swords with Zorro. Watch as the masked champion ricochets from one sticky situation to another in a world where adventure is the name and justice is the game!
name: Zorro

description:
BILLY ELLIOT THE MUSICAL is the joyous celebration of one boy's journey to make his dreams come true. Set in a small town, the story follows Billy as he stumbles out of the boxing ring & into a ballet class, discovering a surprising passion that inspires his family & his whole community. A big musical with an even bigger heart, BILLY ELLIOT will enchant the dreamer in all of us. 

Based on the international smash-hit film, BILLY ELLIOT is brought to life by a phenomenal cast of 45 & the Tony Award-winning creative team -- director Stephen Daldry, choreographer Peter Darling & writer Lee Hall -- along with music legend Elton John, who has written what the New York Post calls "HIS BEST SCORE YET!" 

Please note: only children age 5 and over with tickets will be allowed into the theater for this production.
name: Billy Elliot: The Musical
